newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING WON'T JUMP ON U.S. GAAP BANDWAGON.
newsitem.headline: ING WON'T JUMP ON U.S. GAAP BANDWAGON.

text.p: Dutch financial services group ING NV said on Wednesday it planned to stick with its present accounting principles for its annual report, despite remarks elsewhere that U.S. principles would become the norm.

"Some say that accounting principles worldwide will fall more into line with U.S. GAAP," ING board member Cees Maas told reporters during a press conference at which he gave further details about ING's planned U.S. lising.
"But I expect some principles to develop more in line with European practices as well," he said.
Maas said it would take several more years before companies around the world were using the same accounting principles.

ING noted that foreign companies listed in the U.S. had to prepare accounts in accordance with U.S. GAAP, but added that they could meet this obligation by restating shareholders' equity and profits as reported in their home-country accounts.
"ING Group has chosen the latter option," it said.
ING said it expected year-to-year fluctuations in its results to be greater under U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) than under its own accounting methods.
ING said the treatment of goodwill and the valuation of property, securities and pension liabilities were items that could be affected most by the differences in accounting rules.
